topic: First sensory polish pass for field touch and audio states
currentUserGoal: Make the redesign look and sound less cheap by improving repeated-action feedback and giving run/meta states distinct audio identities.
workCompleted: Added a two-track redesign music state: active runs use lucid-field-theme.wav and Memory Grove uses epic_menu_theme_mellow.wav.
Added a 1.2 second field-to-Grove and Grove-to-field crossfade, including music mute/unmute handling and browser debug state for active track verification.
Added dedicated procedural sound signatures for wound sealing, dormancy collapse, and Last Stand instead of reusing generic UI/regrow sounds.
Moved root touch squash/rebound into the root animation loop so ambient animation no longer overwrites the impact motion.
Reworked touch particles from a perfect radial stamp into varied, upward-biased mixed-texture flecks.
Changed effective-healing feedback from one oversized mote into a staggered three-mote stream toward the Ancient HP bar.
Reduced ordinary touch-burst particle count from ten to eight while adding variation, keeping the repeated effect allocation roughly flat.
Updated the durable redesign document with the music-state split, tactile touch behavior, dedicated event SFX, and current Memory Grove cost wording.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 31 Vitest tests, TypeScript, and Vite production build.
Browser touch smoke confirmed first touch starts the field track, expands the field, and renders the new impact/particle feedback.
Browser state after dormancy confirmed musicMode grove, fieldThemePlaying false, groveThemePlaying true, and Memory Grove visible.
Browser state after Begin Next Run confirmed musicMode field, fieldThemePlaying true, groveThemePlaying false, and active run phase.
Browser console check reported no warnings or errors.
currentGitStatus: Expected after this handoff commit: clean worktree on codex/gameplay-update, four commits ahead of origin/codex/gameplay-update.
knownIssues: Audio quality is subjective and must be judged by the user on their actual speakers or headphones; browser verification can confirm routing and errors but cannot replace listening feedback.
This is a sensory foundation pass, not a full art-direction overhaul. The static HUD panels and broader scene composition can still receive a dedicated visual-depth pass.
The Lucid field source is mono 22.05 kHz while the Grove track is mono 44.1 kHz, so the source recording limits the maximum field-music fidelity.
The playtest run can collapse while browser automation waits because its accelerated drain continues in real time; this is expected on the playtest route.
nextRecommendedSteps: Have the user play one complete run with SFX and music audible, paying attention to ordinary touch, wound seal, dormancy transition, and return to the field.
Use that listening feedback to tune gains and tone profiles instead of adding more simultaneous layers blindly.
For the next visual slice, improve scene depth with restrained field lighting, panel hierarchy, and wound-state contrast while preserving the existing pixel assets.
doNotRevert: Keep field and Memory Grove music as separate stateful tracks unless a replacement soundtrack plan supersedes both.
Keep touch impact motion inside animateScene rather than restoring a tween that animateScene overwrites.
Keep touch flecks asymmetric and avoid returning to the perfect ten-particle radial stamp.
Do not reintroduce the old gameplay loop while restoring its visual charm and sound assets.
